## Natural history notes

A medium-sized tussock moth characterized by mostly white wings crossed by rows of small dark dots, giving it the “dot-lined” appearance, along with a soft, fuzzy body. In Florida, the Dot-lined White is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, parks, yards, and wooded edges where suitable hardwood host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on leaves of trees and shrubs, helping transfer woody plant growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
